item.title: The 11-18 Internet Sabbath - A Cloudflare Outage
item.description:
The 11-18 Internet Sabbath - A Look Back at the Cloudflare Outage

Impact

On November 18, the global network infrastructure provider Cloudflare – jokingly called the cyber Buddha – suffered its worst outage since 2019, with an extremely wide blast radius.

Internet sites relying on Cloudflare services, including famous names such as X, ChatGPT and Claude, plus almost every site of the sort we all know about, all became unreachable.

The outage lasted more than six hours. Rumor has it that Cloudflare engineers could not reach the ChatGPT instance that the outage had taken down, which hurt the speed of the fix. 😂😂😂 That, from another angle, shows just how large the impact was!

How It Unfolded

Back to the starting point. Before 11:05 UTC on the 18th, the sites served by Cloudflare were still enjoying peace and quiet. But from around 11:20, large numbers of sites started throwing “5XX - internal server error” en masse. You could call it a cliff-edge outage.

Even the core CDN, identity verification and the internal monitoring dashboard were unusable.

This bizarre failure pattern made Cloudflare engineers initially assume a large-scale cyber attack, a formidable adversary, perhaps even an attack from the inside. In their internal chat room, people suspected another Aisuru DDOS attack.

So in the early phase a great deal of effort went into hunting this “ghost attack”.

But as the investigation went on, the real cause turned out to be jaw-dropping.

Bot Management

In an era where AI technology is applied at scale, Cloudflare is no exception. It runs a Bot Management module that, using AI machine-learning models, scores security and configuration policies and in turn controls network access.

That model takes a feature file as one of its inputs, and it was precisely this file, used as AI input, that caused this epic bug.

  1. First came routine maintenance work. To improve security, database permissions were adjusted, with the hope of replacing a shared “system account” with “personal accounts” that carry clearer ownership.
  2. That change triggered a latent problem – specifically in the code that generates the “feature file”. That code used to look up the feature list only from the default database, but after the permission change it could suddenly reach another standby database too. And the code never constrained the database source to read from, so every feature got read twice, and the resulting feature file ballooned.
  3. To keep processing efficient, Cloudflare’s bot management module also limits the feature file: the list must not exceed 200 entries.
  4. The bloated feature file blew past that limit and therefore triggered the out-of-memory protection mechanism.
  5. The program crashed, and for safety all service connections were automatically cut.

In short, the root cause was a tiny database permission change!

Lessons

After resolving the issue, the official side immediately reflected and summarized four measures:

  • Harden the ingestion of configuration files generated by Cloudflare so they are as safe as user-generated input files

  • Enable more global kill switches for individual features

  • Prevent core dumps and other error reports from consuming excessive system resources

  • Audit failure modes across all core proxy modules to find the causes of errors

And from a quality perspective, we might ask ourselves:

  1. Why was this kind of permission change applied straight to production? Was it tested at all?
  2. Why did a single point of failure exist, and why did it spread globally?
  3. Why did the exception protection itself crash the program?

Update on the 19th: he has started looking for a new job

What a magnificent amateur-hour outfit….. 😂😂😂😂

item.title: What Can a Test Engineer Do When There Is "Nothing to Test"?
item.description:
What Can a Test Engineer Do When There Is “Nothing to Test”?

As a software test engineer, you have probably experienced this: the developers are still coding, there are no tasks waiting to be tested on the board, no upcoming release, and no regression testing requirements… Especially in the early development stage of a waterfall team, or the early stage of an iteration in agile mode. “Nothing to test” - relaxed, yet a bit idle, with a vague anxiety of wasting your life

But in fact, there is always something to test. Always.

If there are no features to test, there are still many ways we can contribute to product quality: improve the testing process, or improve our own skills as QA professionals.

In fact, these “relaxed” moments can be seen as opportunities for yourself and the project.

Explore the Product in Depth

Use this time to explore the application like a curious user, doing some exploratory testing. Because you have time, you can be more creative and think of scenarios or edge cases you have not tried before. You can also pick parts of the application that are rarely tested and use this time to explore them, checking whether everything there works properly.

You will often find unexpected behaviors that are not exposed in normal testing scenarios. Report everything you find and notify the team. In addition, you can record the scenarios you tried, and later add some of them to the list of all test cases for use in the next round of testing.

Clean Up and Improve Test Cases

Quiet time is a good time to review test cases and check their quality. You can review them:

  • To see whether they are up to date?
  • Whether they are clear and easy to understand. Are there cases that need updating?
  • Are there steps that can be simplified?
  • Are there scenarios you know about but have not yet documented?

This will help when using them in the future. You will be more confident that the test cases are up to date, improved, and provide good test coverage.

Improve Test Documentation

Although it may not be very interesting, it is useful to use this time to review and update any test documentation you have.

Documentation may include test strategy, test plan, test report templates, defect templates, onboarding documents, checklists, and so on.

This is useful because when you need them, you will know these documents have been reviewed and are up to date. They will not be stale documents that lose their usefulness simply because they are outdated.

Create or Optimize Automated Tests

You can use the quiet time to add more automated tests to your test suite. In addition, you can improve your framework structure and optimize existing tests (such as fixing flaky tests, fixing tests that do not work, and improving test steps).

If you are not using any automation tool yet, you can explore which tools can be used for your product, or you can start automating some small, basic scenarios to see how they work before regular use.

Review Past Bugs or Production Issues

Reviewing old bugs or production issues to see what was missed during testing is very useful. This gives you scenario ideas you can use in future testing. You can add these scenarios to test cases or automation suites to prevent these bugs from happening again.

Use this time to learn something from these bugs that will help you in the future.

Explore Other Testing Areas

If you already have some mature performance and security testing, you can review them, explore different scenarios, and see how the application performs in terms of performance and security.

If you do not have such tests, you can explore what tools can be used, check whether they would benefit your project, try some of them, and so on.

Invest in Yourself

Quiet time is a great space for your growth. You can use this time to read QA articles or blog posts, watch tutorials that can help you, try new tools, take courses that help your work, and so on. Afterward, you can present what you learned to the team.

This keeps you inspired, you will learn new things, you will improve, and you will gain new ideas.

Conclusion

As discussed above, even if no one assigns you a testing task today, there is always something to do. By practicing some of these ideas, you will certainly bring more value to the project, the team, and yourself.

As test engineers, our value is not just in executing test cases. Our value lies in our contribution to product quality, our improvement of processes, and our own professional growth.

Even on days that seem “there is nothing to do”, we can find ways to improve ourselves and the team.

Testing never ends, and neither does growth.

item.title: Feeling Marginalized by Your Leader at Work? How to Adjust
item.description:
New to the workplace, I always feel marginalized by my leader, and my state of mind is crumbling — how should I adjust myself?

As the saying goes, nine out of ten things in life do not go as one wishes. Many people new to the workplace brim with ambition but have no chance to display it, and can easily feel overlooked or even deliberately marginalized, leading to an unbalanced mindset and endless frustration.

In this article we briefly discuss this topic.

Are You Really Being Marginalized?

For most people, from childhood through their school years, the path of action was in most cases clear: study hard and you get good grades; whatever you do, the result mostly matches expectations.

But once you enter the workplace and step into society, things are not quite the same. You work hard and act positively, yet the results may not match your expectations. Not only do you fail to earn your leader’s recognition — you may even get a cold splash of water — and it is easy to feel targeted and marginalized.

So, is this really being marginalized?

First of all, you should believe that the so-called marginalization is not a common phenomenon within a team.

People often tend to be self-centered, viewing the things around them from a first-person perspective and focusing on how others respond to their actions. They also tend to act according to their own fixed ways of thinking and understanding — full of enthusiasm, yet not necessarily met with applause.

In fact, if you shift your perspective and look from the leader’s or the team’s point of view, problems are often easy to spot. Is your “hard work and proactive behavior” truly valuable to the team?

Huawei once had a newly hired graduate student from Peking University who, right after joining, wrote a long, ten-thousand-word letter to Ren Zhengfei, discussing at length his suggestions for the company’s future development.

Ren Zhengfei replied — If this person is mentally ill, it is recommended that he be sent to a hospital for treatment; if he is not ill, it is recommended that he be dismissed

Looking at it from the team’s perspective again, in any team resources are always tight, and human resources are especially precious. In reality, no leader likes to put a capable person on the bench.

So in many cases, the so-called “being marginalized” is very likely just an illusion caused by your own sense of letdown. More often, once you find the crux of the problem and make the adjustment, you can move past it.

How to Adjust?

So how do you better adapt to the team and find your place?

It is really what was mentioned earlier — aligning your personal value and the team’s value in the same direction.

If the so-called marginalization is mostly because you have not yet delivered the value you should, then find the corresponding cause and make targeted improvements.

There may be various reasons for not delivering value:

  • Business capability — work hard to improve your professional skills and learn with an open mind
  • Collaboration — in teamwork you cannot be a lone wolf; maintain smooth cooperation with your teammates
  • Personal reasons — put simply, you overrate yourself and are ambitious but inexperienced; you think you deserve a certain position, but your actual ability and influence are not yet up to it

And to determine where the crux lies, besides your own observation and attempts, the more effective approach is direct communication with your leader.

Understand your leader’s (team’s) expectations of you, clarify what your position, the work you take on, and your effective output are, and then make targeted changes.

Really Being Marginalized

Of course, wherever there are people there is a “world” of its own, and we cannot rule out the possibility that you are genuinely considered not worth cultivating by your leader and really are marginalized.

But even so, there is no need to be too discouraged — there is still room.

Because, looking at the different situations of members within a team, being marginalized may not be the worst case.

Within a team, members can roughly be divided into the following types:

  • High-value employees can take charge of key work and core business, and enjoy various incentives tilted in their favor
  • Average-value employees mainly handle routine work, assist in the completion of core business, and receive the team’s normal incentives
  • Low-value employees, that is, “marginalized” employees, usually do peripheral work that does not affect the team’s development and rarely receive incentives
  • Negative-value employees are those awaiting elimination and need to be removed from the team as early as possible

And being marginalized, although fairly dangerous within a team, does not go so far as elimination; it can be said to be in a probationary period.

At this point, through direct communication with your leader, finding where the gap between your own and the team’s expectations lies and making targeted changes, you have a chance to return to the right position.

Naturally, another situation is that through communication you discover the result cannot be changed:

  • The team’s positioning of you is not what you want, and you are unwilling to match the team’s expectations
  • Your personal values and the team’s (leader’s) values differ greatly to begin with — in short, you are not on the same page
  • The constraints on you as an individual are too great, affecting your further development

At this point, either adjust your own mindset and settle into being marginalized — for one without desires there is no weakness — or quietly grow, wait for the right opportunity, build up strength for a later surge, and seek another place where you belong.

Conclusion

All in all, if you feel “marginalized” in the workplace, do not be anxious — in many cases it is not what you think it is. Have a good talk with your superior, find out where the crux lies, and a turning point may well be right in front of you.

item.title: How Is the IT Job Market for 2025 Graduates?
item.description:
The Toughest Job-Hunting Season Ever

The slogan “the toughest job-hunting season ever” is repeated every year, but for the class of 2025, this seems to be no longer just a slogan.

According to Baidu’s forecast data, against the backdrop of year-on-year enrollment expansion in universities, the number of college graduates in 2025 has reached a staggering 12.22 million (compared with 9.54 million newborns in 2024 <2024 Government Economic and Social Development Statistical Bulletin>, the halo of a university degree has long since faded), and the pressure on the supply side of employment has hit a historic peak!

And according to the latest report from Zhaopin, the overall employment rate of college graduates (including flexible employment) is currently only 55.5%. For many graduates, “graduation means unemployment” seems to have become a bitter reality!

A Tale of Two Extremes in IT Employment

With the explosive growth of industries such as AI and intelligent driving, demand in the IT sector remains strong, yet it also clearly shows a trend of polarization! On one hand, emerging fields such as artificial intelligence and cybersecurity are short of talent; on the other hand, traditional internet positions are shrinking, and the competition ratio for some positions exceeds 100:1

IT Is Still a Guarantee of Good Pay

According to data from the 2024 national statistical yearbook, the IT industry, with an average annual salary of 231,800 yuan, has topped the industry pay rankings for nine consecutive years

Falling Employment Rates and Rising Education Barriers

The overall employment rate for computer science undergraduates of the class of 2024 fell to 68.65%, and some universities saw extreme cases of “only 200 out of 600 students employed”. For core positions at major tech firms (algorithm, R&D, etc.), over 60% require a master’s degree, and students from 985/211 universities, backed by university-enterprise collaboration resources, find it easier to land high-paying opportunities. ( Data Source)

Widening Salary Polarization

  • Top tier: algorithm roles at major tech firms pay 400,000-500,000 yuan annually, while top AI talent can earn 800,000-1.5 million yuan a year
  • Ordinary tier: undergraduates from ordinary colleges generally earn a monthly salary of 7K-10K, and some are forced to change careers or “downshift” to second-tier cities
  • Industry comparison: the IT industry, with an average annual wage of 231,800 yuan, has ranked first among all industries for nine consecutive years, yet the average monthly salary of computer science undergraduates of the class of 2023, 6,771 yuan, was overtaken for the first time by electronic information majors (6,802 yuan)

Saturation of Traditional Positions

Java back-end and basic development roles have become a “red ocean” due to fierce competition, with resume submission ratios at small and medium-sized enterprises reaching 8:127. Salaries for junior development positions have fallen back to 8-12K, and many companies have begun to exhibit the phenomenon of “hiring at lower pay”.

Explosive Shortage of High-End Talent

  • Artificial intelligence: the talent gap exceeds 5 million, with a supply-demand ratio of 1:10
  • Cybersecurity: only 30,000 people are trained each year, yet the position gap is as high as 700,000, a gap rate of 95%, and the shortfall is expected to widen to 3.27 million by 2027
  • Hard-tech fields: demand for domestic innovation and local-substitution positions such as chip design and industrial software is growing by 15%+ annually

Self-Help Strategies

So, under such employment conditions, how can current graduates — or students about to enter the job market — break through?

Target High-Growth Fields and Seek Blue-Ocean Opportunities

  • Cybersecurity: obtain the NISP Level 2 certificate (which can be exchanged for CISP without an exam); certificate holders enjoy priority hiring by enterprises and subsidies from local governments
  • AI application layer: focus on real-world scenarios such as autonomous driving, medical imaging, and quantitative finance
  • Hard tech: embedded development (IoT), domestic substitution of industrial software

Build Compound Skills

“Computer Science + X” compound talents earn 20% more than purely technical roles, for example:

  • FinTech (quantitative models)
  • Bioinformatics (gene sequencing)
  • Smart agriculture (sensor technology)

Back Yourself with Hands-On Experience

  • Internships at major tech firms: the conversion-to-full-time rate exceeds 50%, and summer internships have become a core springboard
  • Project experience: high-star GitHub projects, Kaggle competition rankings, and university-enterprise collaboration project experience
  • Certification boost: certifications such as cloud-native (Kubernetes) and penetration testing (CISP-PTE)

Make Rational Regional Choices

New first-tier cities offer outstanding value for money: IT salaries in places such as Suzhou and Xi’an reach 60%-80% of those in first-tier cities, while living costs are 30%-50% lower.

Conclusion

For graduates who stay in their comfort zone and have only a single skill, the 2025 IT job market is undoubtedly a cold winter; but for those who actively embrace change, proactively learn cutting-edge technologies, and develop the ability to solve complex problems, it is also a golden age full of boundless opportunities.

The challenges are real, and the future will always belong to those who take the initiative!

item.description:
In the previous article, we introduced how we used Tencent’s intelligent programming assistant to develop a WeChat mini program that dynamically fetches the hottest open-source tools that emerged over the past month.

Although the first version was put together quickly, it had quite a few bugs; after several hours of continuous tweaking, its functionality is finally more or less working.

The project’s README documentation:

Below are some of the most popular open-source projects from last month. Let us also take a look at which projects are attracting the most attention right now.

1. bytedance/deer-flow

ByteDance’s deep research framework builds a Multi-Agent system on top of LangChain/LangGraph, supporting complex tasks such as automatically generating research reports, PPTs, and two-person podcasts (with the help of Volcano Engine TTS). Its innovations include:

  • Replay mode: Visualizes the multi-turn Agent collaboration process, making debugging and learning easier.
  • Human-AI collaboration: Users can modify AI-generated content in real time through natural language, dynamically adjusting the research direction and details.
  • Efficient architecture: Reduces token consumption through the “Handoffs” mechanism and optimizes the task execution flow.
    Use cases: Automated content generation and academic research assistant. Requires Python 3.12+ and Node.js 22+ for deployment.

In short, it turns AI into a small team that collaborates to complete complex tasks. And you can step in at any time to change its working direction in real time, so you don’t have to watch AI racing off in the wrong direction!

GitHub: https://github.com/bytedance/deer-flow

2. agentcodee/cursor-free-everyday

A tool that cracks the Cursor Pro limitations, solving the feature lockout after the official 14-day trial (such as the GPT-4 call count limit). Its features include:

  • Automatic account management: Get a temporary account with one click and bypass device-binding restrictions.
  • Cross-platform support: Compatible with Windows/macOS/Linux, with a graphical activation program.
  • Free and open source: Community-driven and continuously updated to adapt to new versions.

In one sentence: Bypass the 14-day trial limit of the Cursor IDE and use GPT-4 to write code for free.

GitHub: https://github.com/agentcodee/cursor-free-everyday

3. ngxson/smolvlm-realtime-webcam

A real-time webcam processing tool based on the lightweight vision model SmolVLM (2 billion parameters), designed for edge computing. Its core advantages:

  • Low resource requirements: Preloaded model plus multi-threading optimization lets it run smoothly on low-spec devices.
  • Plug and play: Provides Python/Node.js scaffolding to quickly implement features like object recognition and crowd counting.
  • On-device adaptation: Improves the image token compression ratio by 9x and speeds up inference by 3-16x compared with similar models.

A small 2B-parameter model can run real-time image recognition on an ordinary computer.

GitHub: https://github.com/ngxson/smolvlm-realtime-webcam

4. enescingoz/awesome-n8n-templates (Ecosystem Project)

A template library for the n8n automation tool, providing ready-to-use workflow examples (such as syncing Dida List to Notion). Technical highlights:

  • Event-driven architecture: Flexibly integrates third-party APIs through HTTP nodes and Shell script nodes.
  • Low-cost self-hosting: Supports Docker deployment as an alternative to high-cost solutions like Zapier.
  • Extensibility: Can be combined with the OpenAI API to enhance automation logic (such as automatic email classification).

n8n is a mainstream solution for intelligent workflows, and this library essentially provides a large number of ready-made templates to copy from

GitHub: https://github.com/enescingoz/awesome-n8n-templates

5. ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui

An interaction protocol between AI Agents and front ends, standardizing the communication flow of multi-agent collaboration. Its core features:

  • Event-driven: Defines 16 standard events (such as state sync and streaming messages), supporting SSE/WebSocket transport.
  • Framework compatibility: Seamlessly integrates with Agent frameworks such as LangGraph and CrewAI.
  • Secure routing: Ensures communication security through Secure Proxy middleware.

Through this library, the interaction standards between AI and front-end interfaces are standardized, achieving the advantages of breaking through long waits for AI results and allowing intervention at any time during task execution.

GitHub: https://github.com/ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui

item.title: AI Tips, Generate Images with Local DeepSeek Too
item.description:
We all know that DeepSeek is a text model and has no ability to generate images. Meanwhile, the various online image-generation AIs are either paid or subject to quota limits. Here I would like to share with you a completely free AI image-generation trick using a locally deployed DeepSeek.

The AI Image Generation API

DeepSeek itself certainly cannot generate images at present, but GitHub, that treasure trove, is naturally full of surprises. The image-generation tool introduced in this article comes from a German AI startup and supports text-to-image, text-to-audio, and other functions.

Introduction to pollinations.ai

This project supports image generation through a basic Restful API interface.

Open-source project address:

https://github.com/pollinations/pollinations

Official website:

https://pollinations.ai/

The official website may be plain, but it requires no registration or keys, is open source and free—simply wonderful.

API Definition

The API for generating images is the most basic get method:

1

GET https://image.pollinations.ai/prompt/{prompt}

Parameters supported by the API:

Parameter Required Description Default
prompt Yes Image generation prompt
model No Image generation model used flux
seed No Random seed
width No Image width (pixels) 1024
height No Image height (pixels) 1024
nologo No Whether to keep the pollinations logo false
private No Whether to make the generated image public false
enhance No Whether to use an LLM to enhance the prompt false
safe No Adult content false
transparent No Transparent background (only effective for the gptimage model). false

List of supported models:

  • flux (base model)
  • flux-pro (enhanced effect)
  • flux-realism (realistic style)
  • flux-anime (anime style)
  • flux-3d (3D style)
  • flux-cablyai (unknown)
  • turbo (fast generation)

The http get method can actually be requested and rendered directly through html, which gives us the opportunity to complete image generation based on DeepSeek. In other words, we can define rules that let DeepSeek generate the required prompt and present the image generated by the pollinations api in html according to the HTML format.

Local DeepSeek and cherry studio Configuration

The method of deploying DeepSeek locally via Ollama and interacting with it through cherry studio was described in detail in a previous article [], so I will not repeat it here.

After running the DeepSeek model locally, for example deepseek-r1:14b, open cherry studio, add a role such as Image Generation Assistant, and set its system prompt to define the relevant rules (see the end of the article for the specific prompt).

Next, let’s test it by entering the following in cherry studio:

After some thinking, DeepSeek successfully generated a Picture of Autumn Grass Beneath the City Wall.

item.title: Cursor Charges Money? No Worries, We Still Have CodeBuddy!
item.description:
Previously we introduced generating automated test code with AI, as well as controlling a browser through an mcp server, using the AI programming IDE Cursor. With its powerful intelligent analysis and assisted-programming capabilities, Cursor can automatically complete the code implementation for us when we describe a programming requirement in natural language; it is efficient and works very well. But Cursor is not free software; once the trial period ends, using it as a daily tool is still rather expensive.

But now Tencent has also stepped in and launched a code assistant, the very protagonist of this article, CodeBuddy. Its programming capability is in no way inferior to Cursor’s, and it even has a halo bonus for applications within the Tencent ecosystem such as Mini Programs. More importantly, it is completely free!

Installation

CodeBuddy itself does not provide a standalone IDE, but it offers plugin support for all the mainstream IDEs

Search for “Tencent Cloud Code Assistant” in the plugin marketplace of each development tool and you will find the corresponding plugin; just install it accordingly

Taking VS Code as an example, once the plugin is installed, open the plugin panel and you can get programming assistance similar to the assistant pages of Copilot or Cursor. In CodeBuddy, this is called Craft mode

Besides this mode of assisting with code generation, there is also a Chat mode, which allows conversational interaction much like generative AI.

In addition, Code Review mode helps with reviewing existing code, while Unit Test automatically writes unit test scripts for the current code.

Hands-on Mini Program Development

And since CodeBuddy itself is built on the Tencent ecosystem, for work like Mini Program development it enjoys a natural built-in advantage.

Here, after installing the CodeBuddy plugin in WeChat Developer Tools, with just a few interactive Q&A rounds, it helped me complete the implementation of a Mini Program.

Below is the implementation I completed with it, which fetches the most popular GitHub repositories of the past month. It took roughly a bit over ten minutes in total, and in actual testing it works and the interface is friendly.

item.description:
Preface

In an earlier article about image handling in Markdown documents 【How Should Images Be Handled When Publishing Locally Written Markdown Documents to the Web?】, we introduced the use of AutoHotKey to assist with screenshots and automatic link generation. Some readers sent private messages asking about the concrete usage of this tool.

Below, we will introduce this tool in a fairly systematic way and see how the scripting magic of AHK can make repetitive operations happen with a single keystroke!

AHK Introduction

In software development and technical work that pursues efficiency, repetitive operations often devour precious time. AutoHotkey (AHK), as a lightweight, open-source Windows desktop automation tool, can free users from tedious, repetitive keyboard and mouse operations through concise scripts, significantly boosting productivity.

The key to understanding AHK lies in its scripting language. Core features include simulating keyboard input (Send), mouse operations (Click), running programs (Run), conditional judgment (If), and loop control (Loop), among others. Users need no compilation environment; script files (.ahk) can run directly with extremely low resource usage.

AHK’s application scenarios are extremely broad. Simple ones include auto-filling forms and quickly inserting preset phrases; more advanced ones include batch-renaming files, automated software testing, and customizing dedicated workflows; it can even be used to develop small tools with a graphical user interface (GUI). Its power lies in deep integration with the Windows system, enabling it to manipulate windows, read and write the registry, and access the file system for a high degree of customized automation.

Simply put, AutoHotKey gives users the ability to command the computer with scripts. Whether you are a developer, an office worker, or an everyday user who values efficiency, you can use it to customize your own “shortcut magic,” turning repetitive labor into automation that completes in an instant.

AHK Core Syntax and Common Functions

**Basic Hotkeys

  • Hotkey Definition - Consists of a hotkey followed by a double colon.
1
2
3

^j:: ; Ctrl+J hotkey
 Send, Hello World! ; send text
 return

If there is only a single line of action to execute, return can also be omitted.

Symbol Description
# Win key (Windows logo key)
- Send text after Win is released (Vista+)
- May cause extra simulated keystrokes (see #MenuMaskKey)
! Alt key
- May cause extra simulated keystrokes (see #MenuMaskKey)
^ Ctrl key
+ Shift key
& Combine any two keys/mouse buttons to create a custom hotkey
< Use the left key of a pair (e.g. <!a triggers only with left Alt)
> Use the right key of a pair
<^>! AltGr key (alternate graphic key)
- Represents AltGr combinations (e.g. <^>!m)
- Used alone: LControl & RAlt
* Wildcard: triggers even when extra modifier keys are held
- Example: *#c (Win+C / Shift+Win+C etc. all trigger)
- Forces use of the keyboard hook
~ Keeps the key’s native function (does not block OS events)
- Example: ~RButton (right-click is still sent to the window)
- Affects all combination behavior
- Forces use of the keyboard hook
$ Forces use of the keyboard hook to prevent the Send command from triggering itself
- Has no effect on mouse hotkeys
- Alternative: #InputLevel / SendLevel (v1.1.06+)
UP Triggers on key release (not on press)
- Example: ^!r Up:: (triggers on releasing Ctrl+Alt+R)
- Limitations:
1) Does not apply to controller buttons
2) Must be paired with a normal hotkey to avoid stuck keys

Example

1
2
3
4
5
6

#a::Run Calculator ; Win+A launches Calculator
^!+s::Send Hello World ; Ctrl+Alt+Shift+S sends text
~RButton::MsgBox Right Click ; Message box that keeps the right button's native function
LWin & R::Reload ; Left Win+R reloads the script
*#c::Run cmd.exe ; Any modifier + Win+C launches the command prompt
^!r Up::MsgBox Released ; Triggers when the combination is released

Hotstrings

  • Hotstring - Consists of a colon, zero or more options, another colon, the abbreviation characters, and a double colon.
1

:*:btw:: by the way ; replaces after typing btw and pressing space/enter

Alternatively, you can also use hotstrings to perform somewhat more complex operations.

1
2
3
4

:*:]d:: ; This hotstring uses the following commands to replace "]d" with the current date and time.
FormatTime, CurrentDateTime,, M/d/yyyy h:mm tt ; 
SendInput %CurrentDateTime%
return

Core Commands and Functions

Some commonly used core functions include the following:

Function Name Category Description
FileExist File operations Checks whether a file/folder exists and returns its attributes (e.g. “D” means a directory)
GetKeyState Input detection Detects keyboard/mouse key state, returning 1 (pressed) or 0 (released)
InStr String processing Finds the position of a substring in a string, supporting search from left/right
StrLen String processing Gets the string length (in bytes or characters)
SubStr String processing Extracts a substring starting at a specified position
WinActive Window control Detects whether a specified window is active, returning the window handle (HWND)
WinExist Window control Detects whether a specified window exists, returning the first matching window handle
Format Data processing Formats strings (similar to sprintf)
DllCall System interaction Calls external DLL functions such as the Windows API
Run Process control Launches programs / executes commands (listed in the first draft, full description added here)

Example:

1
2
3
4
5
6

; Combined usage example
if WinActive("ahk_exe chrome.exe") && GetKeyState("Ctrl", "P")
{
FileAppend, %Format("[%time%] Ctrl pressed in Chrome`n")%, log.txt
Send ^{t} ; open a new tab in Chrome
}

Variables and Expressions

  • Variables need no declaration; assign directly (e.g. count := 10)
  • Supports string concatenation (the . operator) and mathematical operations

Practical Use Cases

Case 1 - Automatically Generate Markdown Image Links from Screenshots

Pain point - Manual screenshot → save → copy path → insert into Markdown is tedious Solution - Complete the screenshot and generate a standard link with one key

10
11
12
13

#s:: ; Win+S shortcut
 Run, %A_WinDir%\System32\SnippingTool.exe ; launch the screenshot tool
 WinWaitActive, Snip & Sketch ; wait for the window to become active
 Send, ^+n ; simulate the new-screenshot shortcut (Ctrl+Shift+N)
 WinWaitActive, ahk_class Microsoft.ScreenSketch ; wait for the screenshot to complete
 Send, ^s ; save the screenshot
 WinWaitActive, Save As ; wait for the save dialog
 FormatTime, CurrentTime,, yyyyMMdd_HHmmss ; generate a timestamp filename
 SendInput, %CurrentTime%.png{Enter} ; enter the filename
 Sleep, 1000 ; wait for the save to complete
 clipboard := "![](" . A_Desktop . "\" . CurrentTime . ".webp)" ; generate the MD link
 MsgBox, Markdown screenshot link copied to clipboard!
return

Case 2 - Execute a Complex Command Sequence with One Key

Pain point - Deploying an environment requires repeatedly entering multiple commands Solution - Trigger a command combination with a single key

Case 3 - Automated Test Data Generation

Pain point - Manually creating large amounts of test data is inefficient Solution - Scripts batch-generate structured data

F9::

Summary - Why Use AutoHotKey?

  1. Minimal learning curve - Syntax close to natural language, no compilation environment needed
  2. Resource friendly - Lightweight (installer < 3MB), negligible background footprint
  3. Deep integration - Seamlessly manipulate windows, the registry, and the file system
  4. Rich ecosystem - The official forum offers a vast script library and plugin support
  5. Cross-scenario - Full coverage from text processing to GUI automation
